subject.title: fix(cron): close browser tabs after isolated runs

question: After real runtime evidence is added, should the protected lifecycle change be accepted as the canonical cleanup owner for both scheduled and hook-triggered isolated runs?
rationale: The patch deliberately moves ownership across Gateway and isolated-run boundaries, and the protected label requires an explicit maintainer decision despite the focused implementation.

options.title: Accept shared lifecycle ownership
options.body: Approve after a redacted runtime transcript or log confirms both entry paths close tabs by their detached run-session key.

options.title: Retain Gateway cleanup
options.body: Keep the adapter-level cleanup only if maintainers identify a caller that must retain a distinct cleanup contract.

recommendation.title: Accept shared lifecycle ownership
recommendation.body: Approve after a redacted runtime transcript or log confirms both entry paths close tabs by their detached run-session key.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence routing candidate for the shared cron and Gateway lifecycle boundary.
